summary: Qualitative verification of skill-anchoring-guardrails at 231640d (implementation f621d68 / merge ad00d71) found the candidate satisfies all five capability specs. worktree.Cleanup/Remove fail closed on staged, unstaged, and untracked dirt unless force is true; the four CLI banners fire on the specified triggers and stay silent otherwise; the multi-wave split warning is written to stderr. Test gaps exist around relative/absolute path selection and the accept-failure reminder omission, but they do not break the spec in code.

findings.finding: worktree.Cleanup and worktree.Remove fail closed on all three dirty categories. When force is false, Remove calls PorcelainEmpty (git status --porcelain) and returns ErrWorktreeDirty without invoking git worktree remove, so staged (M /A), unstaged ( M), and untracked (??) trees are preserved. force true skips the check and proceeds to git worktree remove --force.

findings.finding: CLI --force and -f both bypass the dirty guardrail. Unforced dirty cleanup exits 1, prints porcelain plus git diff/status commands citing troubleshooting.md, and leaves files on disk. Clean and nonexistent lanes still exit 0 without --force.

findings.finding: The design's ignored-file false-positive risk is handled by reusing PorcelainEmpty, which already treats a repo ignoring .lucind/ as clean when only .lucind/result.json is present. Root .gitignore ignores .lucind/. There is no dedicated Cleanup/Remove test that unforced cleanup succeeds when only ignored files exist; that behavior is compositional on PorcelainEmpty returning true.
findings.affects: design.md dirty false positives on ignored files; worktree-dirty-guardrail

findings.finding: Threat-matrix Git repository selection is only partially covered by new tests. Invocation inside a linked worktree is a real CLI test (chdir, exit 1, stderr refusal). TestRemoveInvalidPathFailsCleanly uses a non-git temp dir plus an absolute nonexistent path and only asserts err != nil; that would also have failed against pre-change Remove (git worktree remove on a non-repo). There is no test that distinguishes relative vs absolute operator-supplied paths, because cleanup never takes a path argument (pathFor derives it from primaryRoot+laneID).
findings.evidence: TestWorktreeCleanupCLI refuses invocation at cmd/lucind-ai/cli_test.go:3133-3155; runWorktreeCleanup IsLinkedWorktree check at cli.go:1980-1984; TestRemoveInvalidPathFailsCleanly at internal/worktree/worktree_test.go:401-412; PathFor at internal/worktree/worktree.go:159-167
findings.affects: tasks.md Threat-matrix RED tests: Git repository selection

findings.finding: New tests generally assert terminal observables (exit codes, stderr/stdout substrings, file presence, errors.Is) rather than mocked internals. CLI dirty coverage uses only an untracked file; staged/unstaged are covered at the worktree unit layer, not the CLI layer. TestAcceptRequiresExactReceiptAndRendersMechanicalEvidenceOnly asserts the qualitative reminder on success and a non-zero exit on fake verifier error, but after the error path it does not assert stdout lacks the receipt or the steps 2-10 reminder (implementation early-returns before renderAcceptanceReceipt, so the spec scenario holds in code).
findings.evidence: cli_test.go:3039-3072 (untracked dirty CLI), 4685-4690 (accept error checks code==0 only); renderAcceptanceReceipt only reached after Verify success at cli.go:676-681
findings.affects: failure-guidance-banners: Failing mechanical checks exit non-zero without receipt; test quality

findings.finding: dag.Split's new variadic stderr parameter is fail-open: if a caller omits stderr, a multi-wave DAG emits no warning. lucind-ai split always passes stderr, so the CLI spec is met. The pre-existing e2e two-wave test still calls Split without stderr and therefore cannot catch a missing banner.
findings.affects: failure-guidance-banners: DAG split multi-wave base SHA warning banner

findings.finding: RED-then-GREEN is plausible from the diff even though tests and implementation landed in one commit (f621d68). Positive assertions (ErrWorktreeDirty, exit 1, troubleshooting.md, integrate retry, acceptance-promotion.md steps 2-10, stderr recovery-reconciliation.md) would have failed against pre-change Cleanup/Remove (unconditional git worktree remove --force) and pre-change CLI output. Omission tests (Done lane silent, single-wave silent, empty reverted_ids silent) would have passed vacuously on old code; they are paired with the positive tests.
